savedState.boardInfo: This is a deliberately complex example DoView Board. It demonstrates the strengthened V1.2.6 natural-shape, terminal-column guardrail, near-match, and causal-connectivity guidance: a substantial topic is decomposed into distinct domains, causal pathways, implementation workstreams, measures, evaluation questions, and documentation notes without forcing every This–Then page into the same geometry or leaving causal boxes as disconnected inventory items. It is illustrative only and does not use public research. A real board should replace generic assumptions with local evidence and community input.

pageInfo.overview: Reference example only. The varied page geometry is intentional: each page is shaped by its causal domain rather than a repeated grid.
pageInfo.p1: Needs and assets are not treated as a neat four-column pathway because discovery, agreement, and targeting are uneven work.
pageInfo.p2: Household access uses a longer pathway because barriers, affordable choices, stress, and wellbeing are distinct steps.
pageInfo.p3: Supply reliability uses more steps because production, safeguards, continuity, dependable supply, and resilience are different causal moves.
pageInfo.p4: Distribution and service integration is deliberately narrower: the logic turns on roles, routines, and joined-up support.
pageInfo.p5: Participation combines leadership, skills, sustained participation, and ownership.
pageInfo.p6: Governance and learning includes accountability, resources, learning, adaptation, and viability.
pageInfo.p7: How page with implementation workstreams only. Links point upward to relevant This–Then outcomes.
pageInfo.p8: Documentation page for assumptions, evidence notes, and learning guidance.

docContent.p8:
Purpose of this example

This Documentation page shows how a complex DoView Board can keep longer explanation outside compact boxes while still keeping the final board as one standalone HTML file.

Natural-shape note

The This–Then pages deliberately use different numbers of columns and boxes because the domains differ. This is not random irregularity: the need-mapping pathway is shorter, the supply pathway is longer, and governance has its own learning and sustainability sequence.

Assumptions to replace in a real board

  • Local food need, assets, and constraints should be checked with local evidence.
  • Priority groups should be defined with community input and privacy safeguards.
  • Measures should be refined so they are useful and not burdensome.
  • Partner capacity and volunteer load should be reviewed before scaling.

Learning cycle

Use the measures and evaluation questions to revise workstreams, not just report activity. Evidence notes should be added close to the claims they support.

Using DoView Boards and Disclaimer

See the disclaimer section below.

The DoView Board prompt and the DoView Board built within this DoView Board prototype app are provided free of charge so that anyone can experiment with DoView Boards and explore for themselves how they can answer the 20 key questions that anyone running or overseeing an organization needs to answer. See https://doviewplanning.org/doviewboards.

Walk-Through

To get a walk-through for using DoView Boards, see https://doviewplanning.org/walkthrough.

Accessing Consulting or Training

We can provide consulting or training on integrating the use of DoView Boards into your existing planning, implementation and reporting workflows in business, government, or nonprofit settings. See https://doviewplanning.org/offerings.

Adapting the DoView Board Prototype App to your setting

This DoView Board is being used within the DoView Board prototype app. It is a free of charge app that runs inside any browser window and can be used for piloting, testing, proof-of-concept and for use where confidential information is not being included and where there is a low security risk.

The DoView Board app is an open-source developer project under an Apache-2.0 open-source license. See https://github.com/doviewplanning/official-doview-boards. The wider DoView Planning methodology and DoView® trademarks are governed separately. See https://doviewplanning.org/trademarkuse.

Because it is an open-source project, any developer can extend, harden, adapt, or include features of the DoView Board app in other planning products or systems to suit specific deployment requirements. For example, adding enhanced stability, scalability, security, authentication, data handling, or integration features needed for production use, sensitive content, or higher-security environments. If you are looking to deploy DoView Boards in a live operational setting, you can work with any developer to tailor the app to your needs. You can also get in touch with us for advice and methodological input into the best way for you to adapt and extend your use of DoView Boards in your particular setting. https://doviewplanning.org/contact.

Disclaimer

DoView Boards are provided for planning and illustrative purposes only. The content of any DoView Board does not constitute professional advice of any kind, including but not limited to legal, financial, medical, strategic, or organizational advice. No warranty is given as to the accuracy, completeness, or fitness for purpose of any content. The usual precautions for AI-generated material need to be taken. Dr Paul Duignan, DoViewPlanning.org, The Ideas Web Ltd, DoView Corporation Ltd and any associated parties accept no liability whatsoever for any loss, damage, or adverse outcome arising directly or indirectly from the use of, or reliance on, any DoView Board or its contents. Use entirely at your own risk.

Please note that this DoView Board is in an interactive HTML file and contains active JavaScript so the board can work. Only open boards from sources you trust. Read-only copies disable editing through the board interface but are not security protection.

evalQuestions.questionText: Who is still missing out despite the access pathway?
evalQuestions.mainText: Use resident feedback and partner data to identify hidden barriers.

evalQuestions.questionText: Does the initiative protect dignity as well as provide food?
evalQuestions.mainText: Look for experiences of choice, stigma, privacy, and respect.

evalQuestions.questionText: Which supply risks are most likely to disrupt continuity?
evalQuestions.mainText: Review seasonal, storage, transport, volunteer, and supplier risks.

evalQuestions.questionText: Are partners becoming better coordinated or just busier?
evalQuestions.mainText: Check whether coordination reduces duplication and resident burden.

evalQuestions.questionText: Is community leadership becoming broader and more durable?
evalQuestions.mainText: Look beyond attendance counts to shared ownership and confidence.

evalQuestions.questionText: What evidence should change the initiative design next?
evalQuestions.mainText: Use learning reviews to adjust workstreams rather than just report activity.
